instruction: Turn on the 'Do Not Track' request feature in Chrome's privacy settings.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt install jq -y

mkdir -p /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && if [ ! -f /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences ]; then echo '{}' > /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences; fi && cd /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && jq '. + {"safebrowsing":{"enabled":false,"enhanced":false}}' Preferences > temp && mv temp Preferences

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated Chrome menu -> Settings -> Privacy and Security -> Security. Found Safe Browsing section with Standard protection appearing selected. Model concluded it was already enabled and stopped without making changes. Evaluator returned 0 because safebrowsing was disabled in Preferences.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open Chrome three-dot menu, navigate to Settings, click Privacy and Security sidebar, navigate to Security subsection, read and understand settings options
metadata.failure_analysis: Model misread UI state - saw Standard protection radio button as selected but safe browsing was actually disabled via Preferences config. Did not click to toggle/enable the setting.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a different privacy toggle (Do Not Track) that requires navigating to Privacy and Security settings - within demonstrated capability. Tests the model's ability to actually toggle a setting switch rather than just navigate to it.
metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling the Do Not Track feature in Chrome privacy settings. Evaluator restarts Chrome and checks the enable_do_not_track preference, expecting 'true'.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter 'get_enable_do_not_track' correctly reads Chrome Preferences JSON and checks 'enable_do_not_track' key, which is the correct preference key for the Do Not Track feature.
Metric 'exact_match' correctly compares the getter's string output ('true'/'false') against the expected value 'true'.
Expected value 'true' is semantically correct for verifying that Do Not Track has been turned on.
Postconfig properly restarts Chrome to ensure Preferences file is flushed to disk before the getter reads it.
Single-requirement instruction is fully covered by the evaluator - no missing checks.
